name: Name
body: Battle Forge is a monthly series that presents a new WARMACHINE scenario in each installment. Battle Forge scenarios emphasize the narrative unfolding over the course of a game and may be asymmetrical, uneven, and even somewhat experimental because the goal of Battle Forge is to create a sandbox toolset that allows for creative scenario generation and new, story-worthy experiences with WARMACHINE! Players are encouraged to modify Battle Forge scenarios in any way that makes the scenario more appropriate for their army collections and their available terrain resources. Most important of all, have fun! And if you find a better way to do something with a scenario that results in a better experience for you, let us know at feedback@privateerpress.com, so we can try it, too!

name: Name
body: Following are the key terms that will be repeated in many Battle Forge scenarios:

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models, uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective, uncontested.

name: Name
body: Battle Forge victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set amount of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body: If a player makes an attack that destroys one or more friendly models, that player’s opponent gains 1 Victory Point. If a player makes an attack and destroys their own Leader model, that player immediately loses the match.

name: Name
body: In addition to objectives, Battle Forge scenarios will routinely draw on the following terrain elements. Dimensions provided are approximations, and you should feel free to substitute any terrain pieces you have available as necessary. Use the resources you have available to get close enough to maintain the spirit and intention of the scenario.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 3/4" x 4". Barriers provide cover.

name: Name
body: Obstructions with an approximate footprint of 5" x 5".

name: Name
body: Forest areas with an approximate footprint of 5" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 2" x 2". Small obstacles provide cover.

name: Name
body: An elevated platform at least 1" above the table, such as a hill or terrace. Plateaus can possess multiple areas at different heights that models can be placed on, but the areas must be level to prevent models from falling over. If a model cannot be placed on a level area without risk of falling off, it cannot occupy that area. Models cannot be placed on slopes, and we recommend that plateau terrain with sloped surfaces not be used. Plateau, Small—A plateau platform with a footprint approximately 6" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 30 mm models to be placed on. Plateau, Large—A plateau with a footprint approximately 6" to 12" in diameter and a level surface(s) at least 1" above the table that is large enough for five 40 mm models to be placed on.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 4" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of rubble approximately 6" in diameter.

name: Name
body: A 3" x 5" trench template.

name: Name
body: The Guard Tower has ARM 20 and 40 damage boxes. The Guard Tower has the following special rules: Building: This terrain feature is a building. Habitable Guard Tower: Small- and medium-based warrior models can enter this building through a door on the lower level. A model/unit ending its Normal Movement within 1" of the door can choose to enter this building. Models entering this building can be placed on either the lower or upper levels. Models in a unit occupying this building can placed on either floor or both. There can be up to five small-based models or three medium-based models on each floor. There must be room for a model’s base for it to be placed on either floor. Movement Inside the Guard Tower: Models/units can use their Normal Movement to be placed on the top floor if they were previously on the lower floor or to be placed on the lower floor if they were on the top floor. Units using their Normal Movement to be placed are considered to have moved. Models cannot otherwise move or be placed while inside the building.

name: Name
body: Top Floor: The upper level of this building is considered to be elevated terrain. Additionally, arcane and ranged attacks made by models on the top floor gain +4 RNG.

name: Name
body: The enemy of your enemy is your friend. Until he’s your enemy again…. So, watch your back!

name: Name
body:
"Cutthroat" is an adaptation of one of our Summer of Plunder Legendary Event scenarios held this year at Gen Con and is designed specifically for three players using 50- or 75-point forces.
Multiplayer games can be a bit tricky, and you should expect a three-player game to last significantly longer than a normal two-player game, especially with the ability to redeploy models, which is part of this scenario. But the additional element of diplomacy (and backstabbing) that naturally occurs in three-way matches, as well as the chaos of each player having a different set of objectives, makes "Cutthroat" a great format when you’ve got three friends together and want to throw down a game of WARMACHINE.

name: Name
body: "Cutthroat" ends after one player has achieved their victory condition.

name: Name
body:
Each player takes on the role of a different agenda with a specific objective: Invader, Plunderer, or Defender. Feel free to choose agendas or to roll off for them, but each player must take on a different agenda.
Each player has a War Chest of coins that can be spent on War Chest advantages, including boosts to combat rolls as well as redeploying lost models. Players start with 10 coins each and can acquire more during the match by securing treasure objectives.

name: Name
body: Defender: Destroy two Invader and two Plunderer Rally Points. Invader: All Guard Towers and Bunkers are destroyed. Plunderer: Capture the Cargo before the buildings are destroyed by moving it to a Rally Point or deployment zone. .

name: Name
body:
Place 4 small forests, 2 small plateaus, 4 small walls, and 4 small obstacles on the table as shown as in the map below. Also place 2 Bunkers, 2 Guard Towers, and 1 small building (Command Center). If you don’t have this exact assortment of terrain, use what you have to create a diverse environment with an emphasis on terrain that blocks line-of-sight across long distances.
Place four Rally Points marked by flags around the Command Center that CANNOT be destroyed.
Invaders and Plunderers have two Rally Points marked by flags, which CAN be destroyed. Four Cargo objectives should be placed in the Invader’s deployment zone.

name: Name
body:
Before the game starts, Invaders cannot place defenses within 5" of a Guard Tower or Bunker.
Defenders can destroy an Invader or Plunderer Rally Point by securing it.
Invaders can place a Fire Pit or Powder Keg defense within 1" of any building during any turn that they dominate the building by having more models within 1" of it than any other opponent does.
Additionally, Invaders may place one Powder Keg Defense within 1" of any building that they secure, even if they do not Dominate it.
When a Powder Keg explodes within 1" of a Building, that Building suffers 20 points of damage.
NOTE: Invaders both securing and dominating a building may place a total of two Powder Keg Defenses within 1" of that building.
Additionally, a Guard Tower is destroyed at the end of any round if there are two Fire Pits within 1" of the Guard Tower. Fire Pits within 1" of a Guard Tower that is destroyed are removed from play.
Additionally, a Bunker is destroyed at the end of any round if there is a Powder Keg on top of the Bunker and no other models are on top of the Bunker.

name: Name
body: Plunderers can place a Cargo objective within 1" of a building on a turn they secure it. Plunderer Cohort models can use their combat action to pick up one Cargo objective if they begin their activation within 1" of it and can then place it within 1" of the Cohort model at the end of their activation but are -1 SPD while carrying the Cargo. Cargo within 1" of a building when it is destroyed is eliminated and removed from the table.

name: Name
body: Treasure objectives award d6 coins when secured. After a treasure objective is secured, remove that objective and randomly determine the position of a new treasure objective by rolling a d6 and placing it according to the map below. If the treasure objective that was just secured was on a blue point, place the new objective on an orange point, and vice-versa. If a treasure objective already exists on a point that is rolled, the player with the least number of model points in play may place the new objective on any unoccupied point of the appropriate color.

name: Name
body: 1 coin: A player can boost the attack and/or damage rolls of one model or unit for one turn. Any number of models or units can be boosted in a single turn. X coins: On their Maintenance Phase, a player may redeploy any one model or unit that has been destroyed or removed from play to one of their Rally Points or their original deployment zone by paying the point cost of the model or unit in War Chest coins. Leader models may be redeployed for 10 coins. Each time the leader is redeployed, the cost in coins increases by 10 coins.

name: Name
body: Each agenda has a different victory condition: Invaders Win when all Guard Towers and Bunkers have been destroyed. Plunderers Win when they capture four Cargoes. Defenders Win when they destroy all four Invader and Plunderer rally points.

name: Name
body: Feel free to modify this scenario to suit your gaming group’s needs. Consider setting a turn limit if time is limited because as noted earlier, this is going to be a long game. You can also eliminate the War Chest mechanic and treasure objectives, but this will make it easier for a player to be shut out of their ability to achieve a victory.
